correctness.rationale: For every block \(j\), a base \(j\)-colouring of \(K_{m_j}\) without a monochromatic triangle exists by \(m_j<R_j(3)\). The first-differing-coordinate rule prevents a monochromatic triangle: if the first nonconstant coordinate has three distinct values, the base colouring rules it out; if exactly two values agree, the equal pair receives a later-block colour. The count \(P_{j-1}e_{j,c}Q_j^2\) gives colour density at most \(((m_j-1)/(P_{j-1}m_j))(N_L/(N_L-1))<2/P_{j-1}\). Finally, \(\log P_{j-1}=(1/8)j^2\log j+O(j^2)\), while \(i\log i=j^2\log j+O(j^2)\) throughout block \(j\), proving the stated decay and the unbounded sequence of countercolourings.
